title: Limbic vs. Prefrontal Control: Analyzing Emotional Decision-Making
description: Evaluate how prefrontal top-down inhibition modulates amygdalar bottom-up emotional reactivity during acute dilemma scenarios.
problemStatement:
In an experimental behavioral economics study, participants must decide whether to accept or reject an unfair financial offer ($1 out of $10) in an Ultimatum Game.

### Your Mission:
1. **Neurocircuitry Conflict**: Analyze the competing activation between the anterior insula / amygdala (bottom-up emotional disgust) and the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (dlPFC, top-down cognitive calculation of self-interest).
2. **Phineas Gage Comparison**: Predict how a patient with bilateral ventromedial prefrontal cortex (vmPFC) damage would behave in this game.
3. **Fear Extinction**: Explain how the infralimbic / ventromedial prefrontal cortex normally suppresses conditioned fear memories stored in the amygdala, and why vmPFC hypoactivity is observed in Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD).
hints: Hint 1: vmPFC damage impairs the ability to integrate emotional somatic markers with rational cost-benefit decisions.
Hint 2: In PTSD, the prefrontal 'brake' fails to downregulate amygdalar hyperreactivity.
